transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Markus (Gelato Lead ML Eng), Sana (Gelato Infra), Ethan (Gelato PM)

Summary: quick sync, focusing on KV/prefix hit-rate fixes and a canary plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh — quick roll call, and then Priya will go through the telemetry.
[00:18] Markus (Gelato): Hi all, Markus here. Sana and Ethan on my side. Thanks.
[00:25] Priya (SE): Hey team, good morning / afternoon. I pulled the last 7 days of cache metrics, should be visible in the sheet link in chat.
[00:32] Sana (Infra): saw the link, yep.
[00:36] Priya (SE): Ok, so headline — global KV hit rate is sitting at about 16% median, with bursts up to 28% on specific endpoints. Prefix-level hit is worse on long conversational flows — single-digit for some prefixes.
[00:52] Markus: wow that's lower than we expected, we were hoping for 40% with the reuse heuristics.
[00:57] Priya: yeah, so quick diagnosis — two big things: one, eviction policy TTLs are very aggressive, many entries get evicted after ~30s due to our default window; two, prompt surface area is variable — we saw many small token differences (timestamps, session ids embedded) that break prefix matching.
[01:15] Jordan: okay, can you show an example?
[01:18] Priya: yeah, uh loading slide 3 — here's a sample prefix that had 0 hits despite being semantically same request: differences are micro-phrases like "at 10:00" or user id tokens. Our suggestion is prefix normalization + prompt templating to collapse those variations.
[01:35] Ethan (PM): so are we talking about rewriting prompts on the client or server side?
[01:38] Priya: both are possible. Client-side is ideal long-term, but we can adopt a server-side pre-hash normalization layer to canonicalize common tokens. That buys immediate win.
[01:48] Sana: any perf overhead on that normalization? We're sensitive to tail latency.
[01:52] Priya: negligible if done in C++ path or efficient JS shim — it's a few ms at most. The bigger risk is missing edge cases — we'll start with a small regex set and expand.
[02:05] Jordan: besides normalization, what about eviction tuning? What TTL / LRU mix do you recommend?
[02:11] Priya: for this workload we saw significant benefit when moving from 30s to a 300s soft TTL for conversational flows. Also a hybrid eviction: keep session-affine keys sticky for 5 minutes, then allow aggressive eviction for ephemeral queries.
[02:28] Markus: do we have numbers?
[02:30] Priya: yes — in our internal sim, changing TTLs bumped hit-rate from 14% to 46% for the chat-like routes, though cost went up ~8% due to more long-lived cache entries.
[02:42] Markus: 8% cost seems okay if latency and UX improve.
[02:45] Jordan: do you think canarying is safe?
[02:48] Priya: yep, recommend 2% traffic routing for 48h. Monitor hit-rate, tail lat, and token spend. If stable we ramp to 10% then 50%.
[03:00] Sana: what telemetry should we capture? We need granularity but not PII.
[03:05] Priya: capture prefix hash, route, model version, hit/miss, latency, and a tag for prompt-template id. Strip or hash any potential PII before export — we'll provide a scrubber script.
[03:18] Markus: can you confirm scrubber will remove emails/phone numbers?
[03:21] Priya: yes, basic PII scrub plus option to redact entire user strings. We'll send the script.
[03:26] Ethan: ok. On cost, can you show the guardrails? If TTL increases, token cost goes up right?
[03:32] Priya: slightly — because more cache re-use reduces model token churn but keeping entries longer increases memory footprint on the serving nodes. In our numbers, token spend per request dropped ~10% because reuse avoided re-generation; infra memory grew but within Dedicated pilot limits.
[03:47] Jordan: good. Any concerns about session affinity?
[03:50] Priya: session affinity helps for KV warm caches. If we can keep same instance for a session, hot KV caches are reused and hit-rate jumps. But it reduces load balancing flexibility. We recommended session buckets (small sticky windows) rather than strict per-connection affinity.
[04:05] Markus: what about prompt reuse detection? Some of our prompts include ephemeral timestamps — a better approach might be template extraction at the SDK level.
[04:12] Priya: exactly. We'll give a small SDK patch that tokenizes and replaces known ephemeral tokens with placeholders. That gives major headroom.
[04:20] Jordan: timeline?
[04:22] Priya: plan is: run 48h capture starting Monday, analyze and propose normalization regexes by Tuesday, deploy canary 2% on Wednesday with new eviction policy, monitor 48h, then ramp.
[04:35] Ethan: can you also run a bench on dedicated hardware after canary? We want to compare latency/throughput delta.
[04:39] Jordan: yes we'll schedule.
[04:40] Priya: one more item — we noticed many prefixes are low-volume long-tail keys. A small top-k retention policy (keep top 10% of prefixes hot) plus ephemeral eviction for the rest gives ~30% hit uplift without huge memory cost.
[04:55] Markus: how do we detect top-k? By frequency per rolling 24h?
[04:59] Priya: rolling frequency is fine. We'll produce a top-k list as part of the 48h capture.
[05:05] Sana: any infra changes needed?
[05:07] Priya: minimal — mostly config tweaks: TTL, sticky-window config, and a small normalization layer. If you want on-prem/private we would adapt the same configs.
[05:17] Markus: security review — need SOC2 doc and data handling notes.
[05:20] Jordan: I'll send the SOC2 snapshot and security FAQ after the call.
[05:24] Ethan: great. Quick question — are there known regressions when increasing TTL? Like stale completions?
[05:30] Priya: if prompts mutate quickly, you could serve slightly out of date responses; that's why we tie keys to prompt-template ids and invalidate on template change. Also we have fallback to regen if freshness confidence low.
[05:43] Jordan: any competitor approaches we should be aware of?
[05:46] Markus: we've looked at Anthropic's rep cache model — but they do more server-side canonicalization. We still prefer Redwood's hybrid because of observability.
[05:54] Priya: noted.
[05:56] Jordan: okay, let's capture action items — Priya will run the capture and produce the prefix/top-k export, Markus will sign off on PII redaction, Ethan will enable canary routing, Jordan will send docs and pricing.
[06:10] Markus: sounds good.
[06:12] Priya: quick note — we also found one endpoint with a pathological pattern: session ids appended to prompt title. We recommended adding a pre-hash to remove that segment; patch should be tiny.
[06:23] Sana: we'll flag the SDK team to look at client-side fixes too.
[06:26] Jordan: any final questions?
[06:28] Ethan: nope, thanks.
[06:30] Jordan: cool. I'll follow up with the pricing and the SOC2 link. Priya will drop the capture instruction and scrubber in the shared drive. Meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Agreed 48h telemetry window and 2% canary for eviction policy change.
- Early sim estimated hit-rate uplift from ~14% to ~46% on chat routes with TTL and normalization changes; customer to validate with live canary.
- Small SDK patch recommended to remove ephemeral tokens, but server-side normalization will be used for canary.
- Next sync after 48h canary and initial bench (target ~2026-09-20).

Links referenced: (1) telemetry sheet: https://redwood-internal.example.com/sheets/gelato-telemetry (provided during call), (2) SOC2 snapshot link sent via email after meeting.

End of transcript.
